data.summary: Machine overheat incidents from Jul-Oct 2026 show a mix of false alarms and telemetry‑confirmed events, with outdoor temperature notably higher during overheat events.

findings.claim: Of 100 machine_overheat incidents, 26 were flagged as false alarms, mainly on shifts A and B (E1).
Only 4 of those incidents matched telemetry heat_dissipation_failure=1, while 96 had failure=0 or no match (E3).
Average outdoor temperature at overheat incidents was 24.4 °C, higher than the ~21 °C average for all incident kinds (E4).
Shift B accounted for 40 false‑alarm overheat incidents and shift A for 33, indicating shift‑dependent reporting (E1).
Telemetry data show heat_dissipation_failure is rare (0‑114 per machine over Jul‑Oct 2026) (E2), reinforcing that most overheat alarms lack sensor confirmation.

data.recommendation: Calibrate overheat alarms to require concurrent heat_dissipation_failure=1 in telemetry and review shift‑specific alarm thresholds to reduce false alerts.
